statement: Partition-key routing validates every non-absent operand before applying absent-bound ordering: null/undefined remain valid unbounded sentinels, but unsupported, boxed, exotic, boolean, Symbol and non-finite values paired with an absent key fail closed through the typed mismatch owner; all A1-v5 canonical -1/0/1 ordering, SQLite-BINARY UTF-8, numeric/TEXT compatibility, own-data metadata/table-ID hardening, prototype-pollution defenses, mutable-intrinsic capture and actual consumer ownership remain unchanged.

constraints.statement: Supersedes sealed partition-key-ordering-owner-completion-v5 after the newer category-complete Copilot review on PR #87 rejected the exact v5 candidate: compareRoutingKeys applied absent-key ordering before validating the non-absent peer, allowing invalid/non-finite values such as NaN or Symbol to bypass typed refusal when paired with null/undefined. The earlier lightweight ACCEPT is non-governing; preserve v5 predicate and evidence unchanged.

For compareRoutingKeys, every operand that is not null/undefined is type-resolved and invalid/non-finite values are refused before an absent-key ordering can return. Both directions are covered: invalid vs absent and absent vs invalid.

Null/undefined remain valid unbounded range sentinels. Two absent keys compare equal; absent versus any supported finite number/primitive string/Buffer sorts left; the supported value versus absent sorts right.

The exact accepted parts of v5 remain intact: canonical finite -1/0/1 results, SQLite BINARY UTF-8 ordering, numeric/TEXT compatibility, validation before same-reference equality, own-data iterator-free split metadata, own-data coercion-free merge table IDs, explicit prototype-pollution defenses, isolated mutable-intrinsic controls, and actual KeyRange/PartitionResolver/QueryGroup/split-merge owner expressions.

The v6 witness is run against the exact rejected v5 candidate and must fail at the named invalid-versus-absent assertion while v5's existing focused suite remains otherwise green. The v6 candidate must then make the witness and both v5/v6 doneWhen probes green.
Persisted key type metadata, exact large-integer boundary representation, parser/bind precision, encoding migration and old-boundary revalidation remain A2.
Any v6 src/ candidate requires a category-complete independent verification newer than its last attempt, covering both sealed verificationTemplates and exact candidate fingerprints.
No Raft runtime, consensus transport, lifecycle, membership or formation behavior changes.
